---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Pre-Research Cash Return on Acquisitiveness-Penalized Capital
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(RATIO(MA(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), 3), ADD(at, ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)))))
HYPOTHESIS: The true operating cash generation of an intangible-intensive firm is its cash flow before discretionary research spending, and the honest capital base against which to measure it charges the firm twice for purchased intangibles, so this ratio measures how much cash a firm produces per dollar of capital that actually works.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-5 acquisitiveness-penalized cash return delivered the archive's best Sharpe (0.466) with alpha 4.2% and ls_talpha 3.54 using cash flow alone; adding back R&D makes the numerator economically comparable across research-intensive and research-free firms, which is precisely the accounting distortion this project exists to exploit. It keeps the smooth continuous form that has produced the highest FF5 t-statistics while giving the intangibles theme a role in the numerator as well as the denominator.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Worst-Year Pre-Research Return on Penalized Capital
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(oancf, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), ADD(at, ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)))), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable intangible productivity is the worst-year value of pre-research cash generation per dollar of acquisitiveness-penalized capital: a firm passes only if, even in its weakest year, the capital it truly deployed threw off enough cash to fund its own research program.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive shows two distinct strengths — MIN conjunctions with a five-year floor give strong Fama-MacBeth slopes (fmb 4.6–5.1) while smooth continuous ratios give the strongest FF5 alphas (ls_talpha up to 4.5 with fmb only 1.7) — and this fuses both properties into one variable by taking the floor *inside* the continuous ratio rather than conjoining two ranked legs. If it delivers a high slope and a high alpha simultaneously it is the natural consolidation candidate for the final generations.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Additive Composite of Intangible Lightness and Cash Floor
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at)), TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: If purchased-intangible lightness and cash-flow durability are partially substitutable rather than strictly complementary, an additive rank composite should dominate both the conjunctive (MIN) and disjunctive (MAX) forms because it uses information from the whole distribution of each leg rather than only from the binding one.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: With the same two legs the archive has measured MIN (alpha 5.0%, fmb 4.59) and MAX (alpha 2.9%, fmb 2.95), so the additive middle case is the one remaining operator structure and it directly tests the shape of the interaction rather than restating it. Additive scores also spread firms smoothly, which should repair the flat cross-sectional slopes observed when kinked constructions concentrate their signal in one corner.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Buying Innovation Instead of Building It
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), at), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at))), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that acquire their intangible capital instead of developing it — annual additions to booked intangibles exceeding annual research spending — are substituting deal-making for innovation, and when they also lack a cash-flow floor they are the population most exposed to integration failure and impairment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The two intangible investment channels are compared here as same-unit annual flows, which is a construct the archive has never formed: prior work netted a five-year R&D stock against a booked intangible stock, mixing accumulation horizons. Conjoining the buy-over-build flow with a weak cash floor isolates the specific quadrant where the impairment mechanism should operate, giving a well-populated short leg without relying on subsample restatements of a profitability sort.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Income-Statement Cash Floor Behind Intangible-Light Firms
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), at))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: The economically relevant floor is cash earnings — income before extraordinary items plus depreciation and amortisation — which is measurable for the full history of the sample, so the intangible-light durability result should hold on the much larger population for which a statement-of-cash-flows series does not exist.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every high-alpha archived conjunction is stuck at coverage 0.08–0.09 because it requires five years of oancf, and we cannot tell whether the effect is a genuine broad-sample regularity or an artefact of the post-1988 cash-flow-reporting era. Substituting the income-statement cash-earnings proxy is a measurement change, not a mechanism change, and a comparable alpha at roughly 0.146 coverage would make the final consolidated signal far more robust.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Recent Deal Flow Versus Legacy Intangible Stock
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(TS_SUM(DELTA(ADD(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), COALESCE(intan, 0)), 1), 5), at))), IND_RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(oancf, at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: The penalty attached to purchased intangibles reflects recent acquisitive behaviour — deals still facing integration and impairment risk — rather than a legacy intangible balance accumulated long ago and already validated by years of operations.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every archived intangibles leg penalises the *stock* of goodwill and other intangibles, which conflates a 1998 acquisition with a 2019 one, whereas the five-year sum of additions isolates the live deal pipeline; holding the cash-flow floor fixed makes this a clean decomposition of the archive's most reliable intangibles leg. The answer determines whether the final signal should be built on a stock penalty or a flow penalty, which also matters for turnover since the flow measure decays naturally as deals age.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Pre-Research Cash Return on Acquisitiveness-Penalized Capital---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Adding R&D back to operating cash flow scaled by an asset base is essentially Ball-Gerakos-Linnainmaa-Nikolaev cash-based operating profitability (which explicitly adds back R&D), and the only differentiator from the archived gen-5 signal is the same double-counted-intangibles denominator, making this a known anomaly wearing a one-term modification.

---CRITIQUE Worst-Year Pre-Research Return on Penalized Capital---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Putting the five-year floor inside the ratio rather than conjoining two ranked legs is a genuinely different functional form with a coherent hypothesis, though it inherits the same pre-R&D cash-profitability numerator as the previous proposal and will remain coverage-constrained by the oancf history requirement.

---CRITIQUE Additive Composite of Intangible Lightness and Cash Floor---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is an explicit operator sweep over two legs already tested under MIN and MAX with no new economic content, and it is not even a clean comparison because the legs enter SUMRANK raw rather than industry-ranked, so any difference confounds functional form with the loss of industry adjustment.

---CRITIQUE Buying Innovation Instead of Building It---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The buy-versus-build comparison of same-period flows is a construct the archive has not formed and the negative sign is consistent with the expression (high = acquisitive and cash-weak), though the Δ(goodwill+intangibles) leg overlaps materially with the well-documented asset-growth/acquisition anomaly and the long side of a MIN conjunction will be economically diffuse.

---CRITIQUE Income-Statement Cash Floor Behind Intangible-Light Firms---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A proxy swap rather than a new mechanism, but the diagnosis is correct that oancf history is what binds coverage at 0.08–0.09 (ib-based five-year constructs reach 0.146), so this is a legitimate and decision-relevant robustness test of whether the archive's best result is a sample artefact.

---CRITIQUE Recent Deal Flow Versus Legacy Intangible Stock---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The stock-versus-flow decomposition of the intangibles leg is a substantive and answerable question that the archive has not addressed, but note that TS_SUM(DELTA(x,1),5) telescopes to a plain five-year change in booked intangibles, which sits close to the published asset-growth and acquisitiveness anomalies and should be interpreted with that in mind.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Cash Gross Profit Per Dollar of Knowledge-Augmented Capital
EXPRESSION: IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable intangible productivity is literally output per unit of the capital that produced it: gross profit net of capital consumption, measured against a capital base that includes the firm's self-built knowledge stock alongside its recorded assets, so a firm scores high only if its research has translated into product-market surplus rather than into an expanding expense line.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This drops the cash-flow numerator that made the previous version a relabelled cash-based operating profitability and instead places the intangible capital where it belongs — in the denominator as productive capital — so the score falls, not rises, for firms that spend heavily on research without converting it into margin. The gen-0 attempt at this concept failed only because it used a five-year trend on a degenerate R&D-only denominator (coverage 0.060); the level form with an assets-plus-knowledge base is well conditioned for every firm and should run near 0.14 coverage.
REASONING: It is the batch's only pure productivity construct, complementing the funding-capacity and balance-sheet-fragility channels that dominate the archive.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Research Funded Without Equity Dilution
EXPRESSION: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_SUM(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), DELTA(re, 1)), at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Research programs financed by repeatedly issuing equity transfer value away from existing holders and signal that internal economics do not support the program, whereas the same research intensity sustained without dilution reflects a self-financing innovator; the difference in book equity growth not explained by retained earnings is the dilution channel.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Replacing the flagged operator sweep, this introduces the one financing dimension the archive has never touched — external equity — after cash flow, working capital, total leverage and debt maturity have all been tested, and it is measured as a five-year cumulative issuance rate so it captures a financing regime rather than a single-year event. The interaction is essential: dilution is uninformative for firms with no research program to finance, and research intensity is uninformative without knowing who paid for it.
